about: The zone's ground from a seed (Dom 2026-10-28: Valheim-style world gen, 'no switches, just get everything live in game'). The endless flat plane gets hills and ridges from a pure height(x, z) function (src/zone/terrain.ts): integer-hash value noise (no Math.sin, so every engine returns the same bytes), `octaves` layers each `lacunarity` times finer and `gain` times as tall, `ridge.mix` of it folded into ridges, everything below `level` flat, scaled to `heightMetres`. HEIGHT IS RENDER ONLY: the duel sim stays 2D and flat (src/fight/sim.ts, replays and tests byte for byte); the page lifts the ground mesh, the hero and every foe's root and the camera by height(x, z). FLAT PADS: every place a fight or a rest happens (the pit, the camp where the hero stands again, every boss spawn) is level at height 0 for `flatMetres`, then rises over `blendMetres` (smoothstep), so a fight, its ragdoll and cut pieces, blood and the corpse all stay on the old flat floor and the physics floor (a flat Jolt box at the fighter's own origin) stays valid. A boss pad is at least the boss's leash + aggro + `bossMarginMetres` wide (checked), so a hero dragged to the end of the leash is still on the pad. MAX SLOPE: `maxSlope` (rise over run) is a guarantee, not a hope: the code works out the steepest the rows can ever be (octave gradients + the pad blend) and scales `heightMetres` down to fit, so the effective height can be less than the row (the test prints it). `rings`: the per-ring height multiplier hook (createTerrain's ringMultiplier); data/rings.json is not on main yet, so multipliers is [1] and nothing reads it; `maxMultiplier` is the largest value a ring row may give (the slope guarantee is worked out with it). The mesh (src/zone/terrain-draw.ts) is a square of `mesh.radiusMetres` around the hero, vertices `mesh.gridCellsPerVertex` of the stage's grid cells apart and re-centred in whole `mesh.anchorCells` vertices (so the hills never swim), the old flat floor lowered `mesh.floorDropMetres` beneath it and carrying on beyond, the grid draped on it `mesh.gridLiftMetres` above. The sand-melt (skyview.ts fade) is measured against level ground (`fadeFlat`), so a hill does not melt away because its top is above the eye. With ?ground=v1 or ?postkill=v1 (no zone) there is no terrain. `on` false = the old flat ground.

limits.about: Validation ranges for the rows above.
